why: Both analyses reach nearly the same diagnosis (windfall profits, price-not-cost habit, status culture, exit bars, stop treating import protection as strategy), but Analysis 1 explicitly rules out being the lowest-cost commodity producer and names disciplined contraction as the fallback, which sits closer to the key than Analysis 2's 'world's lowest delivered-cost' ambition. Analysis 2 has the tighter one-screen verdict, but Analysis 1's more specific 90-day actions and leader-first pay cuts make it marginally the better one to hand to the chairman.
